This `exit 1` makes the prewarm a hard gate on every leg that carries it. But a prewarm can only *help* legs that actually build sqlite3 hooks; on legs with no hook to protect it is pure added risk. Concretely:

- **Build web (debug)** failed on this PR's run (07:59:27): `PREWARM FAILED — flutter_app: 1 of 1 targets failed for flutter_app (first: x64-linux: download failed after 4 attempts: HTTP 504 ...)`. Web builds no code assets — the PR's own analysis says so (`nightly.yml`: "web builds no code assets — nothing to prewarm").
```yaml
- name: Prewarm sqlite3 native-assets (bounded retry, gh-2072)
  continue-on-error: true
  ...
  if ! "$DART_BIN" "$SCRIPT_COPY" "${ARGS[@]}"; then
    echo "::warning::sqlite3 native-assets prewarm failed — falling back to the hook's own (single-attempt) download"
```

With `continue-on-error: true` the outcome strictly dominates today's: hook-building legs lose nothing (the hook keeps its own download path when the prewarm can't run), and legs with no hook (web, static, dep-audit) regain their immunity to egress outages.
